posts.text:
47% of Fortune 500 companies run catch-all email, meaning your verifier can't actually tell you if the address you have is real. 

Here's why that matters more than people think.

On a catch-all domain, a normal verifier gets an SMTP "accept" no matter what you send it. So it labels the contact "unknown" or "risky" and you're stuck guessing. Worse: if you send anyway, a dead mailbox on a catch-all domain still gets accepted, then silently dropped. No bounce. Your sender reputation erodes and you don't even see it happening.

Allegrow ran a full census on this, not a sample: they verified the primary domain of every Fortune 500 company, about 4.9 million individual validations (Allegrow's Fortune 500 study, June 2026).

The numbers:
→ 69% run a catch-all setup, sit behind a secure email gateway, or both
→ 47% are catch-all specifically (a conservative floor, since inconclusive domains weren't counted)
→ Microsoft 365 powers 82% of these domains, Proofpoint fronts 80% of the gateways

If 47% of enterprise domains can't be cleanly read by a standard tool, "verified" doesn't mean what most GTM stacks assume it means. 

Here's what that looks like on a real contact. Adobe's domain is catch-all. I ran Stephen Frieder, their Chief Revenue Officer, through Allegrow. A standard verifier would've just said "unknown." Here's what Allegrow actually returned:

Genuinely curious: for those of you selling into enterprise, is this matching what you're seeing on bounce rates, or has it been a non-issue for you?
